block.title: Two bug classes in user glibc's own source: block pointers cast to long int, and a locale loader that trusts the archive
block.p: Both live in the source filnix's stock glibc builds from, so the fixes are three patch files (Upstream-Status: Not submitted, ready to send upstream) applied by a separate mixed build: the stock derivation and its store path stay untouched. First, string/memcmp.c and string/wordcopy.c pass their block pointers to the alignment helpers as long int, and Fil-C drops a pointer's capability at the cast, so a memcmp of 16 bytes or more stops with "cannot read pointer with null object" whenever the helpers are not inlined first: under filcc -O0, and under nanofil at any level. filcc -O2 only works because LLVM happens to inline the helpers. The pointers now travel as op_t *; passing uintptr_t instead traps the same way, because the callee still rebuilds a pointer from an integer. Second, locale/loadarchive.c and loadlocale.c follow the offsets, lengths and counts stored in the locale-archive and category files without bounding them: a full hash table with no match spins the probe loop forever, and the other cases read past the mapping.

tr.td: hash table with no empty slot
six more corrupt archives and files

claim.check: nix build -L -f nanofil/survey/glibc/regress.nix units locarch-stock locarch
claim.p: The units check compiles both string units out of each source tree with filcc -O0 and links them into a driver: the stock units trap, the patched ones pass at -O0 and -O2. The locarch check runs nine crafted archives and category files against a glibc's own libc.so; the matrix above is its verdict for stock and patched. CI runs the units check on every push to nanofil's glibc paths (.github/workflows/nanofil-glibc.yml).

block.p: One harness lesson cost a day of chasing: a program's arguments can choose which archive file the loader reads, but the loader itself comes from whichever libc.so the process maps, so a test must swap the library (LD_LIBRARY_PATH, verified with LD_DEBUG) before it tests a patched glibc. regress.nix's locarch check now refuses to run unless the intended libc.so was really mapped.

The Rocq campaign's fixtures stay captures of the unpatched units: capture.nix's patches ? [] parameter opts in the three patches per capture, and locale/code.sh and MemcmpCode.v will opt in when the campaign regenerates them, so all 155 compiled rocq/glibc files stay cache-hit until then.
